summary.text: AWS starts from deny: every request is denied by default, except for the account root user.
It checks for an explicit deny first, and one deny beats any allow.
Without a deny, a request needs an explicit allow from at least one policy, or it is denied.
Guardrail policies only set a maximum, so the request must also fit inside each one that applies.

pointers.title: Default is deny
pointers.summary: Every request starts as denied. AWS calls this an implicit deny.

anchor.quote: By default, every request is denied.

pointers.title: Root user exception
pointers.summary: The account root user is the one exception. It has full access by default.

anchor.quote: The account root user is the exception

pointers.title: Explicit deny is checked first
pointers.summary: AWS looks through all applicable policies for an explicit deny before anything else.

anchor.quote: AWS first checks all applicable policies for an explicit deny.

pointers.title: Deny beats allow
pointers.summary: If any policy explicitly denies the request, the final decision is deny, even when another policy allows it.

anchor.quote: the final decision is deny, even when another policy allows it

pointers.title: Allow needs an explicit allow
pointers.summary: A request is allowed only if at least one applicable policy contains an explicit allow.

anchor.quote: A request is allowed only if at least one applicable policy contains an explicit allow.

pointers.title: No allow means denied
pointers.summary: If no policy allows the request, the implicit deny stands.

anchor.quote: the implicit deny stands and the request is denied

pointers.title: Guardrails grant nothing
pointers.summary: Service control policies, permission boundaries and session policies never grant permissions by themselves. They only set a maximum.

pointers.title: Fit inside every guardrail
pointers.summary: The request must be allowed by a granting policy and must also fall inside each guardrail that applies.

anchor.quote: it must also fall inside each guardrail that applies

examples.title: Allowed by one policy, denied by another
examples.body: Alex has a policy that allows reading a storage bucket. A second policy explicitly denies it. Result: denied, because an explicit deny wins even when another policy allows the request.

examples.title: Outside the guardrail
examples.body: Jo has a policy that allows reading a storage bucket, but Jo's permission boundary only covers virtual machines. Result: denied, because the request does not fall inside the guardrail.
